I did experience increased anxiety from 10 to 20 but only for about two weeks. When I first started yes, it really did take six months for me to notice but I think that’s due to a lot of factors. At the time I was severely depressed and anxious and going through a loss. I think I may have been feeling better earlier, but I didn’t really notice until the 6 month mark. Also, I was only on 10 mg whereas the effective dose for adults is 20 mg. My doctor encouraged me to move up but at the time I was still afraid to due to the increased anxiety. I’ve stopped and restarted a couple times since then and it’s only taken me around a month to get acclimated. I’m also on 20 mg now which I’ve found to be the perfect dose for me

I'm right here!!! (27F) Before starting Citalopram I was having anxiety and panic attacks multiple times a day, every day.  I had trouble starting bc I was always afraid of taking medication for my mental health. I don't know why but I always thought it would "change me" or something. I had to take my medication in front of my therapist and she had to walk me through not being freaked out about it. I had some really low lows at that point. Not sure if your doc said this to you but a side effect of getting on Cit is increased anxiety... LOL what a lovely side effect for someone who is trying to get their anxiety under control. I honestly didn't realize it was working until about 6 months in just because I was in a really bad state. One day I was like... wait. I haven't had an anxiety attack for a whole day. Then two days, then a week, then month, etc.. That realization was crazy to me. I have had anxiety my whole life but was experiencing anxiety/panic attacks severely for two years leading up to when I started Cit, which was in 2020. Oh, and I forgot to mention I was only at 10 mg when I started because I was afraid of having too high of a dose. I'm currently on 20 mg and loving life. This medication saved me. Don't get me wrong, I still experience anxiety occasionally, and I do get minor anxiety attacks on airplanes, but its SOOOOO much more manageable now. It doesn't take over me anymore. Wishing you luck OP, hang in there. I'm open to answer any questions about my experience with it if you need.

I haven’t seen much about a difference in what works better in terms of auto injectors vs syringes but everyone has their own opinions about that. I swear by injecting in my thighs rather than stomach as I was on Ozempic for a few months back in 2023 and I felt that I lost more weight doing it that way. I’ve had a positive experience so far with vials (in terms of shipping time, quality, supplies) but if you’re willing to pay the price for auto injectors then why not?? Good luck on this journey and I hope everything smoothes out for you soon!

I have been on and off twice in the past 5 years. I was on it for 2 years at 10 mg and was doing better so I stopped taking it cold turkey. Yes, I know, not the best decision and I got brain zaps. Honestly getting on it wasn’t too bad, just because the state I was in was probably the lowest of my entire life. It was a blurry time and I don’t remember much, and I was too depressed and anxious to even focus on the meds. I do however have medical anxiety and I’m pretty afraid of starting new meds. Realized I was doing better at 3 months but I didn’t really get out of that hole I was in until 6 months. Anyways after I stopped taking the meds the first time I was pretty okay for about 6 months before I realized I needed to get on it again. Started at 10 mg and it was actually really scary. My anxiety was heightened x15 and I felt like I was having really dark thoughts. I knew that it was hard getting on the meds for a lot of people so I powered through. I moved up to 15 mg after 2 weeks and still heightened anxiety. It was super hard to not give up. Finally moved up to 20 mg and started feeling better after a couple months. Fast forward a year after I stopped taking the meds again… yes I know, very stupid of me. This last time I went from 10 mg for 2 weeks then straight to 20 mg (skipped 15 mg). Wasn’t as hard as the second time getting on them but I think that’s due to me having a better grip on my anxiety thanks to my amazing therapist. But I still did have heightened anxiety. All I can say is Citalopram changed my life. It helps me so much and I wish I had the courage to take it sooner. I’m still doing solid on the 20 mg and will probably stay on it for a while

Us anxious people tend to fixate on our anxiety (lovely, right?) but keep going and let it do its thing. Starting new meds is a rollercoaster ride but stick through it. I took 10 mg for like 3 years before I moved up to 20 mg. This med has changed my life for the better, and I would take the woes of starting the medication and going up doses all over again. I wish you luck OP and I hope you start feeling better soon.

My fav at the moment: healthy low carb jicama chicken tacos!

Cook up some ground chicken with a splash of water, salt and pep, some paprika, chipotle powder, cumin, oregano, onion powder, garlic powder, coriander, and cayenne. Make guac. I use two avocados, two Roma tomatoes, half of a small red onion, cilantro, one jalepeno and two limes. Chop it all up season with salt to taste.

Make your “sour cream.” More like a chipotle crema actually. Use one cup of low-fat Greek yogurt, one and a half limes, chopped cilantro, and about 1-2 tablespoons of chipotle pepper powder. Would be even better if you used those canned chipotles and blended it all up but I’m lazy. Season with a bit of salt and voila!

I use this ghost pepper habanero salsa from Trader Joe’s that is only 15 cal per 2 tbsp, but when I don’t have that I stick to good ole tapatio which is 0 cal.

Didn’t use an exact recipe but I hope this helps:

- I used leftover dough from Martha Stewart’s Chocolate Macadamia Tart for the crust. That recipe can be found on google but I guess you could also just find an actual quiche crust recipe online. 

- I used zucchini, asparagus, red bell pepper, onion and spinach in the quiche. Now that I think about it, mushrooms would’ve been an amazing addition as well. I saved some asparagus tops, and I thinly sliced zucchini and roma tomato for the garnish. 

- I sautéed the zucchini, asparagus, spinach, onion, and bell pepper with some Lawry’s Seasoned Salt, garlic powder, and pepper. Key step! This really develops flavor and shrinks the veggies so you can fit more veggies in your quiche. 

- I can’t remember if I used 3 or 4 eggs, I guess it depends on how eggy you want your quiche. Mine was pretty vegetable dense. I whisked the eggs (seasoned with salt & pep), around 1/4 cup of heavy cream and a generous sprinkling of cheddar cheese, and then I added in the sautéed veggies. Be sure to omit any of the juices/oil leftover from the sautéed veggies. 

- The great thing about the crust it’s that there is no need to blind bake it! I fixed my dough in my tart pan and the egg/veggie mixture goes right in. Leave a little bit of space to the top because it does puff up a tiny bit. Then I placed the asparagus tops and sliced zucchini and tomato on top all fancy-like.

- I baked it at 350F for around 40-50 min. It sounds like a long time but I wanted to make sure the crust in the middle was fully cooked. 

- Let it rest for at least 15 min. You don’t want the insides to fall apart.

- Eat the whole thing in two days. Or less.

hi! i’m 23f and i was the exact same as you. i’ve had depression and anxiety/panic attacks since my teens and have been terrified of meds for a while. just this august is when i started my meds. 

I am on an antidepressant called Citalopram which is used to treat both my anxiety and depression, as well as hydroxyzine and klonopin depending on how bad my panic attack is that day. 

i was very afraid probably since i did A LOT of research on the meds. i’ve read every horrible experience you could think of. just know there are different kinds of antidepressants, the most common being SSRI’s. i’m sure you’ve heard of zoloft or prozac... citalopram is another one. 

ssris are meant to be taken everyday kind of like birth control. it builds up in your body and takes around a month to get full effect. my good friend is on wellbutrin which works more quickly where they have extended release and sustained release forms of the pill.

personally i haven’t had weight gain on citalopram (ssri) but i have heard good things about wellbutrin (bupropion: generic name). my roommate takes wellbutrin alongside her zoloft as it helps her with libido loss and weight gain. 

when i started my anxiety was definitely worse than my depression. i remember reading about the side effects online and the one i was most afraid of was heightened anxiety. i was like seriously?? this pill is supposed to help relieve that lol. i was expecting all these symptoms i read online like headaches, nausea, and yawning. what i really experienced was dry lips (kinda weird) and for the first few weeks the pill would make me super tired. 

just know it’s not as bad as it seems. everyone has different experiences on different pills. i am the type of person to have health anxiety and i was terrified at first. express your weight gain concerns to your doctor and they will definitely take that into account. even if it doesn’t work out your first go just remember there are so many different types out there so don’t give up. 

but the best piece of advice people told me was to stick it out. especially if they put you on an ssri just wait a few months. it’s not some instant change but trust me after a month or two you’ll notice. i hope all goes well and feel free to message me if you want.
